rationale: Two of the three legs reproduce the archived "Cash-Funded Intangible Compounder" almost verbatim, and the only new leg — (oancf − ni)/at — is the classic Sloan (1996) accruals anomaly, so this is a known-anomaly bolt-on to an existing signal rather than a new mechanism.

The declining-spend-intensity trend leg is a genuinely different economic idea (harvest/operating-leverage phase) rather than a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived margin-inflection signal, though the level leg (high intangible intensity) and the trend leg (falling intangible intensity) partially offset each other and the triple-rank product risks thin, unstable extreme buckets.

By the DuPont identity margin × turnover ≈ oibdp/at, so despite the stated claim to the contrary this collapses to essentially operating profitability × cumulative intangible intensity — i.e., the archived "Capitalized Intangible Yield x Intensity" construction in disguise.

The internally-generated-minus-acquired intangible differencing is a substantively new distinction (not just another profitability × R&D-intensity double sort), though subtracting a goodwill stock from a five-year expense flow is dimensionally awkward and the profitability leg remains heavily overlapped with the archive.

Structurally this is the archived "Lagged Intangible Margin Inflection" with only the intangible proxy swapped (xad + non-goodwill intan for xrd + xad), and the stated rationale is internally inconsistent since COALESCE(xad,0) still stacks all non-advertisers at the bottom of the rank rather than avoiding the arbitrary-bucket problem.

oibdp − dp − xint is just a near-pretax-income numerator, so this is the fourth profitability-level × intangible-intensity double sort in the archive with a cosmetically different profitability definition and no new economic channel.
